_governance.rule: A skill only enters the stack if it (a) is actively maintained (commit within ~90 days, real tests or releases) AND (b) closes a loop no existing skill closes. Duplicate scorers are rejected — they add noise, not signal.
doubt_gate: Taleb — is it maintained, or a dead/fragile repo? (check last commit + release cadence)
Munger — what is the author's incentive? Is the free core crippled bait for a paid upsell?
Fader — does it measure a real outcome, or just a vanity proxy?
Christensen — what job does it do that my current 3 skills don't already do?
Ogilvy — is it grounded in evidence, or marketing claims?
loops_already_covered: WRITE — MYNA-correct content + answer blocks (aeo-seo-agent + aeo_agent.py)
PROVE — real citation verification (geo citations, Perplexity Sonar)
open_loops_worth_filling: AUTHORITY — off-site mention / Reddit / Wikipedia / Wikidata tracking
COMPETITOR — share-of-voice vs named rivals across engines over time
CONTENT-DECAY — freshness / evergreen monitoring at scale
